title: 不 vs 没: two ways to say no
summary: 不 negates habits, intentions, general truths and states. 没(有) negates events and says that something has not happened or does not exist.
pattern: Subject + 不 + Verb / Adjective  ·  Subject + 没(有) + Verb

rules.rule: **不 = not (a general stance).** It negates habits, facts, wishes and the future, and it is the only negation for adjectives. It is not tied to a time.

examples.english: I don't drink coffee.
I won't go to work tomorrow.
This room is not big.

rules.rule: **没(有) = did not / has not.** It negates a completed event or an experience, so it belongs to 了 and 过 sentences. In the negation the 了 disappears.

examples.english: I didn't go to school yesterday.
He hasn't eaten yet.
I've never been to Shanghai.

rules.rule: **有 is negated only with 没**: 没有 means 'does not have / there is not'. Never say 不有.

examples.english: I don't have an older brother.
There are no books on the table.

rules.rule: **Tone change:** 不 turns into bú before a fourth tone (不是, 不去, 不对). It stays bù before other tones. Between a verb and a complement, 不 is neutral: 看不懂.

examples.english: He is not Chinese.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīng bu dǒng tā shuō de huà.
examples.english: I can't understand what he says.

contrasts.text: 'I didn't go' is 我没去; 我不去 would mean 'I won't go / I'm not going'. A past negative with 不 only appears in a habitual or stated-reason context: 他以前不喝酒。
没 is the short form; at the end of a question you must write 没有 (你吃了没有？) or the pair 了…没.

pitfalls: ✗ 我昨天不去学校。 → ✓ 我昨天没去学校。 A past event is denied with 没.
✗ 我没是学生。 → ✓ 我不是学生。 是 is negated with 不, as are adjectives and most mental verbs.
✗ 我不有时间。 → ✓ 我没有时间。 有 only takes 没.
✗ 我没吃了饭。 → ✓ 我没吃饭。 Do not combine 没 with 了.

title: Prohibitions: 别, 不要, 不用 and 甭
summary: Negative commands use 别 or 不要 ('don't'). 不用 says 'there is no need', and 不许 or 禁止 states a ban.
pattern: 别 + Verb  ·  不要 + Verb  ·  不用 + Verb  ·  不许 / 禁止 + Verb

rules.rule: **别 + Verb** is the standard 'don't' in speech. 不要 means exactly the same and sounds a bit firmer or more polite in writing. Adding 了 turns it into 'stop doing it'.

examples.english: Don't talk, he is sleeping.
Please do not smoke here.

examples.pinyin: Bié kū le, méi shì de.
examples.english: Stop crying, it's all right.

rules.rule: **别 / 不要 + 忘了 / 担心 / 客气** produce set polite phrases. Used with 再, 别再 means 'don't ever do it again'.

examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, wǒ huì bāng nǐ.
examples.english: Don't worry, I will help you.
Don't be late again.

rules.rule: **不用** (spoken variant 甭) says that something is **unnecessary**, not forbidden. It is the polite answer to thanks and offers.

examples.hanzi: 你不用来接我，我自己去。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng lái jiē wǒ, wǒ zìjǐ qù.
examples.english: You don't need to pick me up, I'll go myself.
No need to thank me!

rules.rule: **不许 / 禁止 / 不准** express a prohibition by rule, with a forceful or official tone. 禁止 appears on signs.

examples.english: Talking is not allowed during the exam.
No parking here.

contrasts.text: 不要 can also mean 'do not want' in a statement (我不要这个), while 别 is only a command.
别去 forbids going; 不用去 says going is not necessary. Mixing them up changes the message.

pitfalls: ✗ 我别去。 → ✓ 我不去。 别 is only for commands to others (or for oneself in a reminder); a statement uses 不.
✗ 你别去。 (meant: you needn't go) → ✓ 你不用去。 别去 forbids going; 不用去 only says it is unnecessary.
✗ 别谢！ → ✓ 不用谢！ or 别客气！ To wave off thanks use 不用 or 客气, not 别 + 谢.
✗ 别你说话。 → ✓ 你别说话。 别 comes right before the verb, after the subject.

title: Literary negators: 未, 无, 非, 莫, 勿
titleHanzi: 未 / 无 / 非 / 莫
summary: Formal Chinese and set phrases use older negators, each with a clear job: 未 for 'not yet', 无 for 'without', 非 for 'is not', 莫 and 勿 for 'do not'.
pattern: 未 + Verb  ·  无 + Noun  ·  非 + Noun / Clause  ·  莫 / 勿 + Verb

rules.rule: **未** is the formal 没(有) / 还没: something has not happened (yet). It appears in notices, news and compounds like 未成年, 未来, 尚未.

examples.english: This matter has not yet been resolved.
Minors may not enter.

rules.rule: **无** is the formal 没有: absence. It forms many set phrases (无论, 无法, 无关, 无效, 无意).

examples.english: This method is ineffective for him.
We are unable to finish on time.

rules.rule: **非** negates nouns and clauses: 非 + Noun means 'not-', and 非…不可 / 非…不行 mean 'must'. It is the formal counterpart of 不是.

examples.english: This is not for sale.
He absolutely has to go.

rules.rule: **莫 / 勿** give formal prohibitions or warnings: 莫 is also used in proverbs ('let nobody'), 勿 on signs and in notices.

examples.english: No smoking, please.
No entry for those without business here.

contrasts.text: In everyday speech 没有 replaces both 未 and 无, and 不是 replaces 非. The older words are chosen for register, not for a different meaning.
非 only negates nouns directly (非会员); 不是 can negate any clause. Say 他不是会员, but 非会员请登记.

pitfalls: ✗ 我无吃饭。 → ✓ 我没吃饭。 无 is not freely combined with verbs in speech; it fits set phrases like 无法 and nouns like 无意见.
✗ 他是非学生。 → ✓ 他不是学生。 非 is not used after 是; use it in a prefix-like position.
✗ 请莫在这里停车。 → ✓ 请勿在此停车。 勿 is the standard word on notices, 莫 sounds poetic or archaic.
✗ 我还未吃饭了。 → ✓ 我还没吃饭。 未 already negates completion and remains without 了.

title: Double negation for emphasis
titleHanzi: 不…不 / 没有…不 / 非…不可
summary: Two negatives make a strong positive: 'nobody doesn't' means 'everybody'. Chinese uses this to sound emphatic, firm or polite.
pattern: 不 + 不 / 没有 + 不 / 不能不 / 不得不 / 非…不可 / 无不

rules.rule: **不能不 / 不得不 / 不会不** combine a modal verb with a negative: 'can't help but', 'have no choice but'. 不得不 stresses an outside force; 不能不 stresses a moral duty.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ bù néng bù guǎn.
examples.english: I can't ignore this matter.

examples.hanzi: 下雨了，我们不得不取消比赛。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, wǒmen bùdébù qǔxiāo bǐsài.
examples.english: It started to rain, so we had to cancel the match.

rules.rule: **没有 + Noun + 不 + Verb** says 'everybody does': 没有人不喜欢他 = 'there is nobody who doesn't like him'. 无不 is the formal version.

examples.english: Everybody likes her.

examples.hanzi: 听到这个消息，大家无不高兴。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā wúbù gāoxìng.
examples.english: Hearing the news, everybody was happy.

rules.rule: **非 … 不可 / 非 … 不行** means 'must, nothing else will do'. It sounds firm and slightly dramatic.

examples.hanzi: 要学好汉语，非多练习不可。
examples.pinyin: Yào xuéhǎo Hànyǔ, fēi duō liànxí bùkě.
examples.english: To learn Chinese well, you must practise a lot.

examples.pinyin: Tā fēi yào zìjǐ qù bùkě.
examples.english: He insists on going himself.

rules.rule: **不是 … 不 / 不 … 不行** and rhetorical forms: 不是不想 'it's not that I don't want to' (but I can't), and 不去不行 'you have to go'.

examples.hanzi: 我不是不想去，是没有时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú shì bù xiǎng qù, shì méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: It's not that I don't want to go; I have no time.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān de huì nǐ bú qù bù xíng.
examples.english: You have to go to the meeting tomorrow.

contrasts.text: 必须 is a plain 'must'; double negation adds the feeling 'there is no alternative' or politely softens an order.

contrasts.vs: 不得不 vs 不能不
contrasts.text: 不得不 means external pressure forces you; 不能不 means your conscience or duty does not let you ignore it.

pitfalls: ✗ 我不是不喜欢他。 (meant: I like him a lot) → ✓ 我很喜欢他。 A double negation is weaker than the plain positive: it only means 'it's not that I dislike him'.
✗ 我不得不去参加朋友的婚礼，太高兴了！ → ✓ 我要去参加朋友的婚礼，太高兴了！ 不得不 always implies reluctance, so it clashes with joy.
✗ 非去可。 → ✓ 非去不可。 The 不可 must stay; 非 alone is not a modal verb.
✗ 没有人不都来了。 → ✓ 没有人不来。 or 大家都来了。 Do not pile up more negatives than needed; two are enough.

title: Partial negation and the scope of 不
titleHanzi: 不都 / 都不 / 不太
summary: Word order decides what is denied. 都不 means 'none', while 不都 means 'not all'. Adverbs like 太, 很 and 一定 also change when negated.
pattern: 都 + 不 (all not)  ·  不 + 都 (not all)  ·  不太 / 不很 / 不一定

rules.rule: **都不 = none, 不都 = not all.** The negation counts what comes after it. 都 first and 不 second makes every member negative; 不 first and 都 second denies the whole group, but allows exceptions.

examples.english: None of us is going.
Not all of us are going.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū wǒ dōu méi kàn guo.
examples.english: I have read none of these books.

rules.rule: **不太 / 不很 / 不大** weaken an adjective: 不太好 is 'not very good' (polite for bad). 不很 is rare in speech; 不太 is normal.

examples.english: The weather isn't very good today.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú tài xǐhuan chī là de.
examples.english: I don't like spicy food very much.

rules.rule: **不一定 / 不必 / 不见得 / 未必** deny certainty: 'not necessarily'. 不见得 and 未必 are doubtful guesses; 不一定 is neutral.

examples.pinyin: Guì de dōngxi bù yídìng hǎo.
examples.english: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
He won't necessarily come.

rules.rule: **Quantity negation:** 没有一个 / 一点儿也不 / 一次也没 give a total denial with 'not even one'. 并不, 并没有 deny a belief: see the lesson on 并.

examples.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ yí gè rén yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: There isn't a single person in the classroom.
I'm not tired at all.

contrasts.text: English 'All the students don't come' is ambiguous. Chinese is clear: 学生都不来 (none) vs 学生不都来 (not all).
太不 is a strong negative ('very much not'): 太不像话 = outrageous. 不太 is a gentle 'not very'.

pitfalls: ✗ 我不都喜欢。 (meant: I like none) → ✓ 我都不喜欢。 Put 都 before 不 for a total negative.
✗ 他不很高。 → ✓ 他不太高。 In speech 不太 is the normal form.
✗ 我一点儿都喜欢。 → ✓ 我一点儿也不喜欢。 The 一点儿也 / 都 pattern needs a negative.
✗ 贵的不一定好的。 → ✓ 贵的不一定好。 Don't add a final 的 to the conclusion.
